topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks frame the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and introducing the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the molecular signaling cascades and mutations that enable cancer cells to achieve growth signal independence and resist inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells fail to execute terminal differentiation across both hematopoietic malignancies and solid intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through mutations disrupting p53 signaling and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress response
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome proliferative limits by reactivating telomerase and bypassing p53-mediated senescence.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways through aerobic glycolysis, Krebs cycle enzyme mutations, and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the triggers and biological mechanisms by which expanding tumors induce new blood vessel growth to sustain nutrient and oxygen supply.

topics.label: Invasion, dissemination, and metastatic colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multistep progression of cancer cell invasion, vascular transport, and colonization at secondary sites.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarize the collective emergence of cancer hallmarks and conclude the lecture.
